Goals.Goal: Keep the path docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md as a markdown stub: the file exists, it names decisions.xml as the parseable citation index by relative path, and it contains no F/D body. Archives that cite the path or the filename keep resolving. A validator proves the stub exists and that every pre-split F/D token is reachable from it by walking stub to index to id; deleting the stub, the pointer, or one inventory id fails.

Split live content into three genres under docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/, each with a live XML file and a retired sibling: findings, decisions (rulings.xml, because decisions.xml is the index), and a machine-readable registry. D28's three genres and D31's three layers (index / live / retired) are orthogonal. Sweep-remainder registry names (recorded as not work) are not live rows; they are preserved in retired so they are not dropped.

Ship the retirement operation alongside the split, never after. An eligible-and-still-live finding or registry row is an error per entry, naming the event that made it eligible. Each live part has a ceiling computed as ceiling = base + headroom at execution, never transcribed as a scalar of this file. Exceeding a ceiling fails; the message names the retirement operation and must not name a config key as the remedy. Raising a persisted ceiling is not a permitted fix for a red.

Registry source of truth is XML. A live row whose name is a directory under .ngrace/changes/archive/ is an error. The initial retirement pass moves every currently eligible chartered row under that rule. The eligible set is derived at execution, not enumerated here.

Ship the decisions-genre codifiedIn and taughtIn tags as XML elements, each with both resolution checks: an unresolvable pointer is an error; deleting or renaming the named check or pinned skill text is an error while the tag stands. This bundle populates zero historical tags.

Retarget scripts/validate-citation-anchors.ts so the split cannot silently disable it: it remains the validate:citation-anchors member of validate:ci; production invocation with no argv validates the stub at DEFAULT_TARGET and the XML index the stub names; every inventory id is present and unique on the index; a planted missing stub, missing pointer, missing index id, or duplicate index id fails. The qualifier-slug grammar, copy-the-anchor rule, and markdown genre-set cross-file resolver are not ported.

XML identity scheme. Each F/D entry has exactly one id attribute. For every pre-split heading, that value is the delimiter-preserving slug C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR-2 already assigned (F9.1 is f9.1; F21 correction is f21-correction; F19's is f19s). Values are copied, not recomputed. Uniqueness domain is the union of the index and all genre files: each id appears on exactly one RecordIndex Entry and on exactly one body element (live or retired). Duplicate ids are an error. token holds the heading token as written (F161, D28.1); two members of a duplicate heading token share token and differ in id. New entries after the split mint id as the lowercase token; if that id already exists, the new entry takes a qualifier suffix licensed by its title (possessive s, -correction, or -amendment). That minting rule is not a markdown heading parser and is not applied to pre-split entries. Reachability: a pre-split token T is reachable from the stub iff the stub file exists at the cited path, the stub names decisions.xml as the index by relative path, and the index contains an Entry whose id is T's assigned slug and whose token is T. The stub does not enumerate every token (that would recreate the dump). Ids are not reassigned. Heading tokens are not rewritten.

Stub contract. decisions.md exists, is markdown, and is a pointer, not a fourth dump: it names ./decisions.xml as the parseable index, may name the live genre files and the registry, and contains no F/D body and no heading that matches the F/D tokenizer ^#{1,6} [FD]\d. Failure to exist, to name the index, or to keep every inventory id reachable via the scheme above is an error of the citation-anchor validator, with planted refuse paths. Do not delete the path. Do not put bodies in it.

Genre XML bodies. Machine-read fields are XML attributes or elements. No fenced metadata block anywhere. Finding carries id, token, status="live|retired", optional PaidBy child (a C-* directory name), Title, and Body. Decision carries id, token, status="live|retired", Title, Body, and optional CodifiedIn / TaughtIn children. CodifiedIn is kind="lint-rule" with a catalog id, or kind="test-suite" with a repo-relative test path. TaughtIn is path plus section attributes. Status matches the file: live files contain only status="live"; retired files only status="retired". Body is the pre-split body as XML character data (entities < > &), decoded for hashing. The immediately preceding HTML <a id name> line is not part of the body; it becomes the id attribute. The ATX heading line becomes Title. Bodies are moved, not rewritten, except that wrap and the Title/id split. In-body ](#slug) destinations stay as ](#slug); the identity validator resolves them against index ids, not against same-file headings. Do not rewrite them to a markdown path. Do not add, rewrite, or delete a finding or decision body beyond those allowed transforms.

The "code it describes no longer matches" half is not machine-checked here; it stays a brief instruction. Initial PaidBy population is the registry Pays column of delivered or superseded rows plus archived spec sentences that call an F-id "the paid finding". Decision eligibility. A live decision that carries a CodifiedIn or TaughtIn child whose pointer resolves is eligible and still live: an error per entry, naming the tag. This bundle populates zero historical tags, so the initial pass moves none under this rule. The checks still ship, with planted refuse paths.

Ceilings, live parts only, D30 dynamic derivation. The tool measures base at execution during this bundle's retirement pass, after the initial eligible moves, and persists ceiling = base + headroom. Bases are never transcribed here. Live findings: base = line count of findings.xml at that moment; headroom = 7 times the median line-count of a live Finding element at that moment. Live rulings: base = line count of rulings.xml at that moment; headroom = 2 times the median line-count of a live Decision element whose pre-split heading was H2, at that moment. Live registry: base = live row count at that moment; headroom = 15 additional live-row slots (a policy constant, not a measurement of decisions.md). Citation index: base = line count of decisions.xml after the split; headroom = 40 lines (a policy constant). Failure text names retire / move to the retired sibling, never a config key, and says raising the persisted ceiling is not the remedy.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-PATH-SURVIVES: After apply, the path docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md exists, is a markdown stub rather than the pre-split dump, names ./decisions.xml as the parseable index, and contains no F/D body. bun ./scripts/validate-citation-anchors.ts exits 0 on the production stub. Deleting the stub, removing the index pointer, deleting one inventory id from the index, or duplicating an index id makes it exit non-zero. Every pre-split F/D token is reachable from the stub by the identity scheme in Constraints. Failure: the stub exists by convention with no refuse path; reachability is inspection.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-IDS-KEPT: Every pre-split F/D heading's assigned id is the id attribute of exactly one RecordIndex Entry and exactly one body element. Heading tokens are unchanged. Ids are not reassigned. Failure: a missing id; a rewritten token; a new id on a pre-split entry; HTML <a> copied into a Body; a {#id} suffix.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-PRESERVATION:
bun ./scripts/prove-record-preservation.ts exits 0 against record-inventory.json: every pre-split F/D heading occurrence is present on the index with its assigned id, and every whitespace-normalized decoded body hash is present in the union of the four genre body files. A reviewer re-runs this command; inspection is not evidence. Failure: a missing heading token, a missing or reassigned id, a missing body hash, or a command that only prints ok. The test file plants a missing inventory body and a missing heading token.
bun test scripts/prove-record-preservation.test.ts

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-FINDING-ELIGIBILITY: A live finding whose PaidBy names a directory under .ngrace/changes/archive/ makes the retirement validator exit non-zero, one error per finding, naming that archive event. AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CEILINGS: Live findings, live rulings, live registry row count, and the citation index each have a ceiling computed at execution as ceiling = base + headroom from the formulas in Constraints.
